node.title: Re: Replacing a module dependency
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
[mod://MIME::Lite] [https://metacpan.org/dist/MIME-Lite/source/lib/MIME/Lite.pm#L2861|uses] a harcoded require Net::SMTP;, so you can't tell it to use something else without modifying its code (or perhaps using an [doc://@INC] hook, but that's fairly advanced and not something I'd necessarily recommend over the following). One possible approach would be to place your own version of [mod://Net::SMTP] in [doc://@INC] before any other paths with e.g. [doc://lib]. However, this requires your version of Net::SMTP to also be called Net::SMTP, which means you'd need to copy Net::SMTP and modify it... personally, I actually think your suggestion of making a new module that inherits from [mod://MIME::Lite] to be more elegant than that!

However, note in general you probably want to consider switching to one of the newer Email::* modules by [https://metacpan.org/author/RJBS|RJBS], the current maintainer of [mod://MIME::Lite] - the documentation of that module starts with:

MIME::Lite is not recommended by its current maintainer. There are a number of alternatives, like Email::MIME or MIME::Entity and Email::Sender, which you should probably use instead. MIME::Lite continues to accrue weird bug reports, and it is not receiving a large amount of refactoring due to the availability of better alternatives. Please consider using something else.
